title: Template Observability explainer diagram for docs (request flow + spans/metrics)
creator: Talia Benson
description: Create a simple diagram/visual for the docs site that explains (a) the request flow in the RAG+Agents quickstart templates and (b) the spans/metrics/log fields emitted by default (OTel + Redwood conventions). This should help users verify instrumentation and help Support/SRE explain what to look for in traces and dashboards.
content:
## Context
We’re adding Quickstart Templates docs + prebuilt dashboards. Users keep asking: “What spans/metrics should I see?” and “Where is latency coming from (retrieval vs tool vs LLM)?”

This ticket produces a single, reusable diagram that can be embedded in:
- Docs walkthrough for RAG+Agents template
- Observability hooks reference
- README snippets (as an image link)

Source of truth for naming:
- Confluence: Quickstart Templates Observability Hooks Standard (OTel + Redwood conventions)
- Confluence: Quickstart Tracing Conventions (Templates)

---

## Goal
A diagram that a user can understand in <60 seconds that answers:
1) What happens on a request?
2) What spans are created (high-level hierarchy)?
3) What metrics are emitted (names + what they mean)?
4) What IDs correlate logs ↔ traces ↔ Redwood Support (redwood.request_id)?

Non-goals:
- Full “how to set up OTel” instructions (covered elsewhere)
- Provider-specific or vector DB vendor deep dives
- Showing any sensitive payloads (prompt/doc/tool args)

---

## Diagram requirements
### Must-haves
- Simple left-to-right flow with 6–8 boxes max.
- Clear separation between:
  - Template app (user’s service)
  - Dependencies (vector store, tools)
  - Redwood API
  - OTel Collector / export path
  - Dashboards (Redwood Console / user backend)

### Span labels (use exact names from current template standard)
Show as callouts on the flow (not a full tree):
- `redwood.quickstart.request` (logical root for template work)
- `redwood.rag.retrieve` (retrieval)
- `redwood.agent.loop` (agent orchestration)
- `redwood.tool.call` (per tool invocation)
- `redwood.llm.request` (call to Redwood; streaming spans until completion)

Include a small “example trace shape” inset (text-only) to avoid forcing users to interpret the arrows as a strict parent-child model.

### Metrics callout (names + short meaning)
Include a compact “emitted metrics” list (5–8 bullets) with the prefix to make it obvious these are template metrics:
- `redwood.quickstart.request.duration_ms` (end-to-end)
- `redwood.quickstart.llm.duration_ms` (LLM call duration)
- `redwood.quickstart.llm.ttft_ms` (streaming TTFT)
- `redwood.quickstart.llm.tokens.total` (total tokens)
- `redwood.quickstart.rag.retrieve.duration_ms` (retrieval latency)
- `redwood.quickstart.tool.call.errors` (tool errors)
- `redwood.quickstart.streaming.disconnects` (streaming reliability)
- `redwood.quickstart.errors` (taxonomy-coded error counter)

### Correlation + safety callout
Small note box (1–2 lines each):
- Correlate with: `redwood.request_id`, `trace_id`
- Safety: “No prompt/doc/tool payloads in spans/metrics by default (only counts/lengths).”

### Visual style
- Works at 680–760px width in docs.
- High contrast, friendly but “engineering docs” aesthetic.
- Must render in light + dark docs themes:
  - Deliver both light and dark variants OR single neutral variant that works on both.
- Use Redwood brand colors sparingly (avoid looking like a marketing graphic).
- Avoid tiny text; minimum 12–13px equivalent when exported.

---

## Proposed layout (approved)
**Title:** “What the template emits (traces + metrics)”

**Main flow (left → right):**
1) Client / Browser / Caller
2) Template App (FastAPI/Express)
   - callout: `redwood.quickstart.request`
3) Retrieval (optional)
   - Vector Store
   - callout: `redwood.rag.retrieve`
4) Agent loop (optional)
   - Tool execution
   - callouts: `redwood.agent.loop`, `redwood.tool.call`
5) Redwood API
   - callout: `redwood.llm.request` (includes streaming + TTFT)
6) OTel SDK → OTel Collector
7) Redwood Console dashboards (and optional customer Grafana)

**Insets/callouts:**
- “Example trace shape” (3–6 lines)
- “Metrics emitted” bullet list
- “Correlation IDs” mini box

---

## Deliverables
1) SVG (preferred) + PNG fallback for docs.
2) Dark mode asset (if needed) with the same geometry.
3) Alt text (docs-ready) and a short caption.
4) Small source file handoff (Figma) with layers named (so DevEx/Docs can edit text later).

---

## Acceptance criteria
- Diagram uses the current span names/metric names from the Observability Hooks Standard.
- No high-cardinality examples (no prompts, doc IDs, user IDs) appear in the graphic.
- Allison (Observability) signs off on naming and redaction note.
- Elliot/Wei sign off on docs readability and text length.
- Asset exported and referenced by docs PR (or attached for Wei to integrate).

---

## Open questions
1) Do we show OTel Collector as “local dev docker-compose” or generic “collector/exporter”? (Decision: generic box, with a small “local dev” label.)
2) Do we mention template telemetry tagging header? (Decision: no; too footgun-y, and not needed to understand spans/metrics.)

---

## Updates / decision log
- 2025-02-12: Initial wireframe drafted (boxes only). Feedback: too many elements; reduce to one vector store + one tool box.
- 2025-02-18: Added explicit span name callouts and a tiny example trace inset. Allison requested exact span strings match template standard.
- 2025-02-24: Added metrics list; Sergio requested we include `ttft_ms` and streaming disconnects since those drive the shipped dashboards.
- 2025-03-04: Final copy edits for “Correlation IDs” box; changed phrasing to: “Use `redwood.request_id` to open a Support ticket.”
- 2025-03-14: Exported final SVG/PNG (light + dark). Handed off to Wei for docs integration.

---

## Reviewer notes (captured)
- Allison Grant: “Keep span names exact; do not include prompt/doc content anywhere. Add a one-liner that attributes are counts/lengths.”
- Sergio Costa: “Include TTFT and streaming disconnects; those are the top ‘why is streaming weird’ questions.”
- Christine Wong: “Make sure it’s legible at docs width; reduce text in the main flow and move detail into the side callouts.”

final_alt_text: Diagram showing the request flow for a Redwood quickstart template: a client calls the template app, which optionally performs retrieval and agent tool calls, then calls the Redwood API. The template emits traces with spans like redwood.quickstart.request, redwood.rag.retrieve, redwood.agent.loop, redwood.tool.call, and redwood.llm.request, and exports metrics (request duration, LLM duration, TTFT, tokens, retrieval latency, tool errors, streaming disconnects) via OpenTelemetry to dashboards. Correlation uses trace_id and redwood.request_id; no prompt or document payloads are emitted by default.
final_caption: How quickstart templates generate traces and metrics (and where to look in dashboards).
